As an IT Specialist (System Analysis) "Product Manager", GS-2210-14, you will be responsible for: Leading the development of FSA products by understanding the needs of students, families, and stakeholders, translating insights into product roadmaps, prioritizing high-impact features, and measuring success by user outcomes.

Serving as the bridge between policy goals, technical systems, and user needs by translating complex constraints into actionable requirements and ensuring compliant, secure, and user-friendly solutions at national scale.

Collaborating and aligning with contractors, partner agencies, and cross-functional teams to align efforts with the product vision, hold vendors accountable for outcomes, and deliver tangible improvements for users.

Fostering a product culture of experimentation, data-driven decision-making, and continuous improvement while providing vision and expert recommendations that align government staff and vendors around shared goals for students and families.

Applying deep experience building and managing products at scale to ensure FSA systems deliver accurate, secure, reliable, and seamless experiences while protecting sensitive personal and financial data.
Minimum Qualification Requirements You may meet the minimum qualifications for the GS-14, if you possess the specialize experience.

Specialized Experience for the GS-14: One year of experience in either federal or non-federal service that is equivalent to at least a GS-13 performing two (2) out of three (3) of the following duties or work assignments: Experience serving as the product expert in the development of a scaled technology platform.

Experience serving as a product manager, overseeing internal and external software development, testing, integration, and operation. Experience communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences and translating business requirements into technical user stories.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) The quality of your experience will be measured by the extent to which you possess the following knowledge, skills and abilities (KSAs).

You do not need to provide separate narrative responses to these KSAs, as they will be measured by your responses to the occupational questionnaire (you may preview the occupational questionnaire by clicking the link at the end of the Evaluations section of this vacancy announcement).

Knowledge of product management principles, with a focus on user-centered design and measurable outcomes. Skill in translating policy and technical requirements into intuitive, scalable product solutions. Skill in managing vendors and cross-functional teams to deliver results and drive tangible product improvements.

Ability to inspire and sustain a mission-driven product culture and drive collaborative efforts amongst the teams. Knowledge of building and operating large-scale, mission-critical systems or comparable technology infrastructure.

At 1KOMMA5° , we pursue a clear vision: Living on wind and sunlight forever for free . To make this a reality, we are building the energy system of the future with Heartbeat AI. Want to be part of it?
We bring together regional craftsmanship and scalable software: We don't think of solar, batteries, heat pumps, and e-mobility as isolated components, but control them as an intelligent, integrated overall system in our virtual power plant. Directly connected to the electricity market – in real time, fully automated.

This way, energy is used when it is available from renewables and particularly cost-effective. By 2030, our goal is to transition 1.5 million households to renewable energies. Over 3,000 people are working towards this every day, at more than 80 locations worldwide, from Finland to Australia.
Want to take responsibility and build solutions that truly matter? Apply now and help us shape the energy world of tomorrow.
Learn about our Product & Tech team!
Deine Position
As Product Manager Procurement & Portfolio Management, you take on one of the most strategically defining product roles within our energy retail business: you design how 1KOMMA5° procures, hedges, and optimizes electricity for an increasingly flexible customer portfolio. You sit at the intersection of energy markets, energy procurement, our flexibility assets, and our customer-facing tariff strategy - and you turn this into a measurable commercial advantage.
Own our Procurement Strategy: Define how and where 1KOMMA5° procures energy for our customer portfolio - across day-ahead, intraday, and forward markets. Develop a clear market split logic, and continuously refine it based on portfolio characteristics, customer mix, and market conditions.
Design Portfolio Hedging & Risk Management: Build hedging and risk management strategies tailored to different customer portfolios (dynamic vs fixed tariffs or flexibility/ancillary services). Define when and how we lock in volumes, what we leave open, and how we balance commercial upside against risk exposure.
Shape Our Flexibility Procurement Model: Design how we procure and steer our flexibility portfolio. Defining models such as flexibility bands, fixed volumes, strike-price-based offers, and the trade-offs between them. Develop the commercial logic and the operational requirements for each model.
Run Quantitative Portfolio Analysis: Independently run analyses on procurement performance, hedging effectiveness, and portfolio economics. Build the analytical foundation that supports strategic decisions, identifies optimization opportunities, and quantifies the impact of changes to our procurement and steering setup.
Monitor Performance and Drive Continuous Improvement: Define KPIs across procurement cost, hedge effectiveness, portfolio risk, and flexibility margin. Use data to continuously sharpen our market positioning and commercial performance.
Dein Profil

4+ years of experience in (international) energy procurement, portfolio management, or energy trading, ideally in a utility, energy retailer, trading desk, or aggregator environment
Strong analytical skills with hands-on experience running portfolio analyses, hedge calculations, and market scenarios (Python, SQL, or comparable tools are a strong plus)
Proven ability to translate market and commercial logic into structured processes and product requirements
Entrepreneurial, proactive, and comfortable navigating ambiguity in a fast-moving market environment
Excellent written and spoken English and German

Deep understanding of European power markets - day-ahead, intraday, and forward markets - and the mechanisms that drive prices
Solid working knowledge of hedging instruments (futures, options, OTC), balancing markets, and BRP settlement
Familiarity with flexibility products and procurement models (flexibility bands, fixed volumes, strike-price offers) and their commercial trade-offs
Awareness of regulatory frameworks shaping energy retail (Marktkommunikationsprozesse, balancing regimes, market design developments)
Experience working with external procurement partners, ETRM systems, or trading platforms is a strong plus

You are part of an international, dynamic, and highly motivated team of people who have proven to make things happen
With your work, you accelerate the "energy transition" and hence have a direct impact on our climate
Work with and learn from other super-smart colleagues
You will enjoy direct contact with core decision-makers
You will enjoy the best chances of entering full-time in one of Europe's most thriving scaleups
You can work in one of our offices in Hamburg, Berlin or Munich
Create a healthy balance alongside your work and enjoy all the benefits of the EGYM Wellpass

Better Money Strike is the Bitcoin company. With Strike , you can buy and sell bitcoin, pay bills, and borrow against your holdings. From individuals to businesses, Strike is purpose-built for every step of the Bitcoin journey.

Available in more than 100 countries — including the U.S., Europe, Latin America, and Africa — Strike is building a better financial system powered by Bitcoin. Bitcoin is better money. Strike is how you use it. Role: Strike is where people around the world send, save, and spend money on bitcoin rails.

For a product like that, customer trust is a feature in and of itself.

As Trust Product Manager, you'll own the features that make customers confident keeping their money with Strike : account security controls, verified support experiences, beneficiary planning, account management, and the systems like KYC/B, transaction limits, account restrictions that keep fraudsters out without getting in the way of good customers.

You'll ship customer-facing features, and you'll own the foundations underneath them, turning what most companies treat as friction into experiences customers actually appreciate.

You'll succeed by shipping trust-building features customers love, minimizing fraud, maintaining compliance, and protecting the health and integrity of the Strike ecosystem. This position is available for candidates located in the eastern US time zone.

What You’ll Do: Serve as the voice of the customer (internal customer too!) and intimately understand the products we offer as well as their potential fraud vectors and blind spots Work closely with Compliance, Finance, Operations, and Data to uncover and understand needs Partner with cross-functional peers to define, prioritize, and deliver a roadmap and product that maximize impact to financial risk management and our fraud strategy Own our Fraud KPIs and partner with Data and Finance to iterate on their definition as needed Establish and track success metrics for various features and initiatives, including operational efficiencies Support and motivate cross-functional teams through an inclusive and collaborative mindset Qualifications: At least 4 years of experience in product management, with at least 2 of those years in trust/fraud related teams A highly experimental mindset to drive innovation amidst uncertainty or ambiguity (e.g., new processes, teams, systems) Vast experience working with designers and user researchers Empathy to work with a diverse array of cross functional peers and stakeholders Resourcefulness, pragmatism and roll-up the sleeves mentality Excellent verbal and written communication skills Experience and interest for Bitcoin and Fintech is a plus US-Based Positions Salary range: $162K - 190K Equity in a high-growth startup Health, dental, and vision insurance premium contributions; short & long-term disability insurance and basic life insurance Cell phone and internet reimbursement Flexible PTO, sick leave & parental leave Access to a company 401k plan We do not make hiring decisions based on educational history whatsoever.

Our Founder is a college dropout. We employ high school dropouts, PHD candidates and everything in-between. We do not hire credentials. We simply hire talented, passionate individuals who are excited to be a part of our team.

StackAdapt is the leading technology company that empowers marketers to reach, engage, and convert audiences with precision. With 465 billion automated optimizations per second, the AI-powered StackAdapt Marketing Platform seamlessly connects brand and performance marketing to drive measurable results across the entire customer journey. The most forward-thinking marketers choose StackAdapt to orchestrate high-impact campaigns across programmatic advertising and marketing channels.
The Creatives team is on a mission to build a one-stop-shop for advertisers' creative production and management needs.

We're developing a comprehensive in-house product that lets clients create, enhance, preview, store, and manage CTV, video, audio, DOOH, display, and native ads at scale — whether they start from ready-made templates or build from scratch.

By delivering a robust, full-featured in-house solution, we reduce our clients' reliance on costly third-party creative providers and empower advertisers to move faster and more efficiently.
The next chapter for the team centers on AI-powered content generation and a multi-channel creative experience, with particular focus on AI first video and CTV solutions. It's a high-impact, fast-moving area with significant room to define the product, the technology, and the creative workflows that will set the standard for how advertisers build at scale.
As a Senior Product Manager on the Creatives team, you'll own a portfolio at the heart of this ambition. This is a 0→1 space that spans multiple teams and disciplines, and you'll set the direction for it: shaping strategy, making the hard calls, and shipping. You'll partner closely with Engineering, Design, Creative Studio, Data Science, and Revenue to translate a bold vision into products advertisers love.
StackAdapt is a remote first company. This role is open to candidates in Canada and the United States.
What You'll Be Doing
Own the strategy, roadmap, and end-to-end delivery for a portfolio spanning the video/CTV creative builder, AI-generated and brand content products, and creative integrations with social and partner platforms.
Lead 0→1 initiatives from first principles — research and validate the problem, frame the opportunity, define the path forward, and drive it to launch and adoption.
Translate complex, cross-team problems into a clear vision and crisp, actionable requirements that give Engineering, Design, and QE unambiguous direction on how features should behave.
Partner with Data Science and Engineering to shape how AI/ML and generative content capabilities are applied across creative formats, making sound technical trade-offs along the way.
Define key success metrics, monitor KPIs, and make data-informed decisions about what to build, what to cut, and what to double down on.
Work hand-in-hand with Creative Studio to ensure the tooling reflects real creative workflows and produces work that meets a high creative and brand bar.
Build new integrations with external platforms, partnering across teams to open up a wider range of creative assets and ad formats within the creative library.
Communicate precisely and proactively across the organization, keeping stakeholders aligned and informed at the right level and the right time.
Support customer-facing teams by resolving questions about your portfolio and helping triage bugs and regressions as they appear.

s.h: What You'll Bring to the Table
s.t:
Proven experience as a Product Manager at a technology company, with a track record of shipping large, complex software products end-to-end (and you can speak to your successes).
Demonstrated success leading 0→1 initiatives that span multiple teams — you bring structure and direction to new problem spaces and rally others around a clear plan.
Experience building products in AdTech, MarTech, or creative platforms, with a meaningful edge for those who've worked on creative-building or generative AI products.
Strong fluency with AI/ML and generative AI concepts — enough to partner deeply with Data Science and Engineering, reason about capabilities and limitations, and make informed product decisions.
A technical background (Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience) that lets you discuss technical trade-offs, integrations, and architecture credibly with engineers.
A keen design and creative sense, balanced with technical depth — you pair an eye for what "great" looks like with the ability to partner closely with engineering on how to build it.
An excellent cross-functional collaborator who can tailor your approach across Engineering, Design, Creative Studio, Data Science, and Revenue without skipping a beat.
Clear, structured writing and communication — you distill complex ideas into words that build consensus and align stakeholders around your vision.
Strong prioritization instincts grounded in reason, clarity, and purpose — you focus the team on the most impactful work and the KPIs you're moving.
A leadership style rooted in influence rather than formal authority, and the judgment to operate independently in a fast-moving, evolving space.

Die dokSAFE GmbH ist ein Leipziger Softwareunternehmen, das sich auf die Entwicklung der SaaS-Lösung Actaport spezialisiert hat. Wir arbeiten gemeinsam daran, mit unserer Kanzleisoftware die Arbeitswelt in der Anwaltskanzlei zu revolutionieren.
Du willst nicht nur Anforderungen verwalten, sondern ein Produkt wirklich gestalten — nah an Kunden, nah an der Rechtspraxis und nah am Entwicklungsteam? Dann suchen wir genau DICH! Als Product Owner (m/w/d) trägst Du die Verantwortung für die Weiterentwicklung von ACTAPORT von der Anforderungsaufnahme über die Backlog-Priorisierung bis zum Release.

Du übersetzt juristische und gesetzliche Anforderungen in konkretes Produktdesign — und sorgst dafür, dass das, was wir bauen, auch wirklich genutzt wird.
Aufgaben
Du verantwortest die Weiterentwicklung unserer Kanzleisoftware von der Konzeption bis zum Release und behältst dabei Nutzerbedürfnisse, gesetzliche Anforderungen und Produktvision gleichzeitig im Blick.
Du nimmst Anforderungen von Kunden und dem Gesetzgeber auf, analysierst sie und überführst sie in praxis- und benutzerorientierte Funktionen.
Du agierst als enger Sparringspartner für das Entwicklungsteam, um Rückfragen zu klären, Scope zu schärfen, Prioritäten verständlich zu machen und Blocker früh aufzulösen.
Du pflegst und priorisierst das Product Backlog und begleitest den Entwicklungsprozess in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Entwicklungsteam nach agilen Methoden (bspw. Scrum).
Du präsentierst Produktfortschritte gegenüber Stakeholdern, unterstützt bei der Qualitätssicherung und gibst dem Team klares Feedback zu Akzeptanzkriterien.
Du dokumentierst neue Funktionen und schulst bei Bedarf Mitarbeitende und Kund:innen.
Qualifikation
Ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Rechtswissenschaften, Betriebswirtschaftslehre, der IT oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation bildet die Grundlage — entscheidend ist Dein Verständnis für juristische Prozesse und Nutzerbedürfnisse.
Du verfügst über eine Zertifizierung nach CSPO oder PSPO 1.
Du arbeitest strukturiert, detailorientiert und eigenverantwortlich und hast ein ausgeprägtes Gespür für UI/UX.
Du interessierst Dich für digitale Trends, KI und Legal Tech und bringst technische Affinität für Cloud-Software mit.
Deine sehr guten Deutsch- sowie Englischkenntnisse ermöglichen eine reibungslose Kommunikation im Team und mit Stakeholdern, um Ideen effektiv zu teilen und Ziele gemeinsam zu erreichen.

Wir bieten eine sehr gute Work-Life-Balance durch flexible Arbeitszeiten.
Wir leben ein hybrides Arbeitsmodell — Homeoffice ist bei uns selbstverständlich möglich.
Neben 30 Urlaubstagen erhältst Du eine sehr gute Vergütung und zusätzliche finanzielle Benefits (Kitazuschuss, steuerfreier Sachbezug als Deutschlandticket oder 50€-Gutschein).
Wir statten Dich mit modernen Arbeitsgeräten und einer zeitgemäßen Entwicklungsumgebung aus — Du entscheidest, womit Du am liebsten arbeitest.
Dich erwarten flache Hierarchien und kurze Entscheidungswege.
Dich begrüßen erfahrene Teamplayer in einem motivierten, inklusiven Team. Nach Deiner ausführlichen Einarbeitung arbeitest Du eigenverantwortlich in diesem.
Dich erwarten vielfältige Möglichkeiten für Deine persönliche und fachliche Entwicklung sowie eine optionale betriebliche Altersvorsorge.
Werde Teil unseres Teams und revolutioniere mit uns die Arbeitswelt in Anwaltskanzleien. Gestalte Deine Zukunft bei dokSAFE GmbH und bewirb Dich jetzt - wir freuen uns auf Dich!

At DICK’S Sporting Goods , we believe in how positively sports can change lives. On our team, everyone plays a critical role in creating confidence and excitement by personally equipping all athletes to achieve their dreams. We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workforce, reflecting the communities we serve.

If you are ready to make a difference as part of the world’s greatest sports team, apply to join our team today! OVERVIEW: At DICK’S Sporting Goods, our Scorecard membership sits at the center of the Athlete experience—driving engagement, retention, and long-term value.

As we evolve toward a paid membership model , we are seeking a Principal Product Manager to define and lead a step-change in our Loyalty, Membership, and Credit strategy, roadmap, and execution model . This role goes beyond incremental optimization.

You will reimagine the future of Loyalty and Membership , shaping a differentiated value proposition, unlocking new revenue streams, and ensuring seamless integration across our digital ecosystem.

You will lead end-to-end product strategy and discovery for highly complex, enterprise-wide initiatives—working across product, engineering, data, marketing, and external partners to deliver a cohesive and high-impact roadmap. What You’ll Own 1. Step-Change Product Strategy & Roadmap Leadership
Define and drive a bold, future-oriented Loyalty & Membership strategy (including paid membership)
Move beyond incremental improvements to deliver step-change innovation in customer value and business impact
Build and continuously evolve a multi-horizon roadmap (Now / Next / Future) aligned to enterprise strategy
Clearly articulate tradeoffs, investment rationale, and long-term value to executive leadership
Ensure roadmap reflects enterprise dependencies and cross-product integration points

2. Product Discovery Leadership
Design and lead a scaled discovery strategy across multiple product teams and domains
Establish discovery as a continuous, measurable discipline —not a phase

Customer research & segmentation (especially membership behaviors)
Experimentation frameworks (A/B, pilots, pricing tests)
Concept validation for new membership benefits and monetization models

Translate insights into clear product opportunities, business cases, and roadmap decisions

Champion human-centered design and data-informed decision making across teams
Co-lead discovery efforts with Principal UX Design and business stakeholders , ensuring: Customer desirability, business viability, and technical feasibility are equally represented

Facilitate cross-functional discovery workshops that bring together: Product, Design, Engineering, Data, and Business teams

Drive alignment early by ensuring discovery outputs are co-owned and actionable across teams

3. Loyalty & Paid Membership Expertise
Own evolution of Scorecard into a modern loyalty + paid membership ecosystem

s.h: Membership tiers, benefits, and pricing strategy
s.t:
Engagement loops and lifecycle mechanics
Value exchange for Athletes and brand partners

s.h: Bring deep knowledge of loyalty constructs , including
s.t:
Earn/burn systems, rewards structures
Personalization and lifecycle marketing
Subscription/membership economics and retention levers

Evaluate and optimize ROI, LTV, and engagement metrics

4. Digital Ecosystem & Cross-Product Integration
Operate with a systems-thinking mindset —understanding how Loyalty & Membership connects across:
E-commerce & app
Retail store experience
Retail media network
Data & personalization platforms
Marketing technology stack

Partner across product teams to ensure roadmap alignment and coordinated execution

Identify and manage dependencies, integration points, and sequencing risks

Drive shared outcomes across product portfolios , not siloed success
Serve as the central orchestrator across multiple product teams , ensuring Loyalty & Membership capabilities are intentionally embedded across the ecosystem—not layered on top

s.h: Partner with peer Product leaders to
s.t:
Align roadmaps and sequencing across domains
Resolve competing priorities and shared dependencies
Drive shared OKRs and integrated outcomes , not siloed metrics

Ensure consistency in experience, data usage, and value delivery across all touchpoints (digital + store)
5. Enterprise Leadership & Influence
Lead without authority across a highly matrixed organization

Align executives and cross-functional leaders on strategy, priorities, and trade-offs

Executive reviews and roadmap alignment sessions
Cross-functional planning and prioritization forums

Act as a thought leader in product strategy , elevating the maturity of the organization
Act as the unifying leader across Product, Design, and Business , ensuring alignment from vision through execution
Influence not just product direction, but also business strategy and operating models related to Loyalty and Membership

As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges. We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal.

The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved. What you'll be doing
Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.
Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.
Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.
Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.
What you'll need
Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.
Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.
Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).
AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.
Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.
Outcomes
Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap
Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch
Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds
AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted
Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged
Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

We're hiring a Growth Product Manager (Senior to Staff level) to help us achieve our big vision that everyone who makes music has a DistroKid account.
At DistroKid, our product and marketing funnels evolved in parallel. This role unites them and owns the whole picture: member growth end to end, from how artists find us through to how they get value and stay for the long haul. You'll establish where the leverage is, back it with data, and ship.
You'll partner with our staff marketing engineer to direct a small, diligent cross-functional team, and work with them while working across product, marketing, data, and design. This role reports into product and treats marketing as an equal partner in setting priorities.

You'll shape a single growth backlog, balancing measurable wins against the longer-term bets worth protecting. You'll build the framework that sizes every growth opportunity on the same terms, so prioritization performs on evidence and expected impact.

Ideas and market intelligence come from across the company; you turn the greatest of them into instrumented experiments tied to the product roadmap.

Own member growth and the prioritized backlog that moves it, and build the measurement framework the company uses to size and evaluate growth bets
Navigate the full funnel to achieve our growth goals, including acquisition, onboarding, activation, retention, reactivation, and referrals
Conduct experiments end to end: hypothesis, instrumentation, analysis, iteration, and knowing when to stop
Use AI tooling to compress the loop from idea to shipped experiment, multiplying what a small, nimble team can ship
Keep the executive team clear on what you're doing, why, and what you're trading off
Learn from the top consumer growth teams and bring back what works
Help PMs and marketers across the company surface and clear their own growth blockers
Use and iterate on the artist tools and promo assets we already have to build organic and viral growth loops.

5+ years in product or growth, with 3+ years owning a subscriber, revenue, or retention KPI at a scaled consumer or self-serve software company
You conduct experiments at scale, pull your own data, and know the difference between a real result and noise
You've used AI tools to get real growth or productivity gains, not just experimented with them
You have a knack for taking rough, half-formed ideas and turning them into plans a team is excited to perform
You form a clear view of where the opportunity is and change it when the data tells you to
You make complicated things simple and explain them well, including the trade-offs

OKX will be prioritising applicants who have a current right to work in Singapore, and do not require OKX's sponsorship of a visa.
Who We Are
At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.
Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me , Do the Right Thing , and Get Things Done . These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.
About The Opportunity
OKX is expanding its presence across Latin America, and we're looking for a locally embedded Product Manager to drive market growth in the region. This role sits at the intersection of local market strategy and product execution — you'll identify business and product opportunities unique to LatAm, shape how we localize the trading experience, and own the end-to-end user trading journey for the region.
This is not a "translate and ship" role. We need someone who deeply understands how LatAm users discover, onboard, trade, and grow — and who can turn that understanding into product decisions that move our regional metrics.
What You’ll Be Doing
Local Market Opportunity & Strategy
Identify and prioritize business and product opportunities specific to Latin American markets, including regional payment rails, local trading behaviors, regulatory nuances, and competitive gaps.
Build and maintain a deep understanding of the LatAm crypto and fintech landscape — including key competitors, user segments, regulatory trends, and macro factors that influence trading adoption.
Develop go-to-market product strategies tailored to LatAm user segments (e.g., first-time crypto users, active retail traders, remittance-driven users).
Partner with regional BD, marketing, and operations teams to align product initiatives with local growth objectives.
User Trading Journey Ownership
Own and optimize the full user trading journey across APP and WEB — from discovery and onboarding (Markets, Chart analysis) through execution (Order placement, Chart trading, Position management) to post-trade review (Asset analysis, Trading journal).
Define and execute the product roadmap for trading experience improvements in the region, balancing global platform capabilities with local user needs.
Analyze user behavior, funnel data, and feedback specific to LatAm markets to identify pain points and high-impact opportunities for conversion, retention, and engagement.
Develop strategies to serve diverse user profiles — from advanced traders to speculative and novice traders — adapting the product to their distinct preferences and requirements.
Cross-functional Collaboration
Work closely with Design, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to translate user insights into shipped product features and iterative improvements.
Collaborate with UX/UI designers to optimize trading interface layout and usability, ensuring a seamless and intuitive experience.
Partner with Engineering to ensure efficient feature implementation, maintaining a balance between innovation and operational feasibility.
Measure the impact of product initiatives through well-defined metrics, using data-driven insights to refine strategies and deliver measurable outcomes.
What We Look For In You
5+ years of product management experience with a demonstrated track record in consumer-facing product, ideally in trading, fintech, or crypto.
Solid understanding of manual trading workflows across mobile and web — including the needs and behaviors of different trader personas.
Strong ability to translate user research and local market insights into actionable product roadmaps.
Excellent product sense, attention to detail, and a history of shipping products that users love.
Strong analytical skills — comfortable working with data to prioritize, validate hypotheses, and measure outcomes.
Proven cross-functional leadership — able to align design, engineering, data, and commercial teams around a shared vision.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas clearly to diverse stakeholders.
Nice-To-Haves
Proficiency in Spanish and/or Portuguese. Candidates who can engage with LatAm users and stakeholders in local languages will have a strong advantage, though this is not a strict requirement.
Direct experience in the Latin American market — understanding of local user behaviors, payment ecosystems, regulatory environments, and cultural nuances across the region.
Hands-on trading experience in FX, stocks, or crypto.
Familiarity with technical analysis tools and charting platforms.
Experience working in globally distributed teams with cross-regional collaboration.

Various team building programs and company events
Wellness and meal allowances
Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

It also needs a working knowledge of the constraints across marketing, sales, customer success, finance, accounting, legal, and privacy, plus a deep understanding of who our athletes are and how they actually use our products.

That depth comes from genuine curiosity: about the business, about the families and athletes we serve, about the data behind their behavior, and about the technology, including AI, that shapes what's possible for the product.

This role sits at the bleeding edge of solving problems for families navigating the college recruiting process.

The decisions made here will shape the experience for thousands of families, and in some cases change the course of a young athlete's life. It's an individual contributor role, accountable for solving real problems for customers in a way that works for the business, not just shipping a list of features.

Success here is measured by the outcomes we create for athletes and families, and by how those outcomes move the business forward.

s.h: Your Mission This is a company built for growth, not comfort.
s.t:
When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone.
We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences.
Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform.

Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users.

At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in.
If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.
What You’ll Own: Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.
Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.
Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.
Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.
Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.
Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.
Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.
What Success Looks Like: You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.
Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.
Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.
Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.
You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.
You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.
What You Bring Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.
Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.
Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.
Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.
Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.
Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.
Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.
Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.
How We Win Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.
Please note: this is not a remote only position, we offer you a flexible hybrid model here in Hamburg, Germany - working from home on Mondays & Fridays, coming to the office on Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday!

TL;DR — alago brings AI-powered project management to the construction industry. As our Product Manager , you'll own a core product area end to end: how messy project data becomes an early warning that a €200M project is about to go wrong. Full-time, Munich.
About alago
Imagine if building a building were as easy as building software. Every moving part visible, every change traceable, every decision still carrying its reasoning six months later.
Software got there by making its own history legible — every commit, every diff. Construction never did. A €200M project runs on plan sets nobody can diff and decisions buried in email, so the same mistakes happen over and over, and the industry loses $1.6 trillion a year to it.
That's what we're fixing. Eleven people, 15+ customers, €1M+ pre-seed from leading construction-tech VCs and one of Germany's largest project developers. The product is live and used daily on real construction sites — which means the interesting work is only starting.
Tasks

Translate deeply technical construction workflows into decisions engineers can build from
Own a product area end to end: From discovery on site to shipped, instrumented, measured features
Shape the roadmap: Balance what the next customer needs against the foundations that make the next ten cheap
Make the hard prioritization calls on scope and sequencing, and defend them
Define what "working" means: pick the metrics, instrument them, read production data, iterate
Treat LLM behavior as a product problem, not a research one — evals, fallbacks, and what the user sees when the model is wrong

Must-haves
2+ years shipping product — as a product manager, or as a UI/product designer who's been making product calls and not just screens
You've shipped something where the hard part was the data model, not the button
Hands-on experience with LLM-powered features in production — you know what breaks and how users react when it does
Genuine willingness to put on boots and go on site until you know the domain better than we do
Bonus
AEC background
Founder experience, or product work at a company under 20 people
You already build your own agents and internal tools to do your job faster
Not a match on every line? Apply anyway — potential and learning curve count.

You'll be one of our first product hires, which means you own critical parts of the product end to end and work directly with the founders. It's early enough that you help decide how the company works, and the path from here goes to either top individual contributor or leading product as we grow, depending on where you're strongest.

A lean team and a flat structure. High independence and end-to-end ownership: you take a problem from discovery to launch to measurement yourself, without layers of approval in between.
Your users sit next to you. Our advisors and CSM team are the people your product serves, so feedback comes in hours rather than after a research cycle — and you see the effect of what you shipped almost immediately.
Big scope, real impact. Three brands and one shared financial picture — a wide surface for a team this size, and decisions that visibly move the business.
Fast pace. We ship, learn and correct quickly instead of planning quarters in advance.
Profitable, bootstrapped and proven. Eight years on the market, 500,000 customers, and we fund ourselves — so the roadmap follows customer value and business sense, not the next funding round. You also get real scale of data to work with.
Genuinely hard problems. Optimisation across lender rules, tax logic, risk and long-term financial outcomes, plus AI and automation applied to a regulated, high-stakes process.
How we work — and who thrives here

s.h: This will be a good fit if you
s.t:
Take initiative by default. When something is unclear or broken, you go and find out, rather than waiting for a decision to arrive.
Solve problems from first principles. You dig into messy, ambiguous situations, form your own view of the root cause, and propose a way forward.
Learn fast and enjoy it. Mortgages, German regulation, lender logic, our internal systems — a lot to absorb, and you will be expected to get up to speed largely on your own.
Handle context switching. On any given day you may move between an AI experiment, an advisor workflow bug, a lender requirement and a data question — and hold several threads open at once without dropping them.

s.h: It probably will not be a good fit if you
s.t:
Prefer one clearly scoped project at a time with minimal interruption.
Want a defined process, an existing playbook, and clear direction on what to work on next.
See the PM role mainly as writing tickets and coordinating rather than digging into the domain and the numbers yourself.
Are uncomfortable making decisions with incomplete information, or need consensus before moving.
First 6 months — what success looks like
Month 1–2: You know the mortgage process end-to-end, have shadowed advisors on real cases, and can articulate the core pillars of our workflow.
Month 3–4: You own a defined area, have a prioritised roadmap for it, and have shipped at least one improvement with a measurable effect on advisor efficiency or conversion.
Month 5–6: You are the go-to person for your domain, running discovery independently, and one AI/automation initiative is live and demonstrably reducing manual work per case.

We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the Teramind Endpoint Agent, and the AI Usage Control capabilities built on top of it, end to end.

You will be the single accountable product leader for the roadmap, priorities, and outcomes of the Agent organization - approximately half of Teramind engineering, working across operating systems, low-level platform components, and the server-side telemetry pipeline. This is a pivotal role.

The Agent is one of the strongest competitive moats Teramind has, and the next chapter of the product strategy depends on what we build into it. You are coming in to bring product rigor, customer insight, prioritization discipline, and technical judgment to a team that is capable of shipping world-class endpoint technology.

AI Usage Control is one of the most important things you will build here. Companies have spent twenty years governing what employees do with sensitive data, and they now have a second workforce: AI agents reading files, calling tools, and executing commands on the same machines, with none of the accountability.

Nobody has worked out what supervising them looks like, and much of it never touches the network, so the endpoint is the only place you can see it. You will own that end to end. You will sit alongside other product managers, reporting to the VP of Product. Together, you own Teramind's product surface area.
What You Will Own
The Agent roadmap across all platforms. Windows, macOS, Linux, and the platforms after them. You decide what ships, in what order, and why, balancing customer demand, platform modernization, performance, and security hardening on one prioritized backlog.
The endpoint layer of AI Usage Control . Detecting AI that never touches the network - native desktop clients, IDE-embedded assistants, terminal-based coding agents, AI-native Teramind | Senior Product Manager, AI and Endpoint browsers, and local models running offline - and capturing the prompts, pastes, uploads, and agent-executed commands that browser and network DLP cannot see.
Translating business vision into engineering reality . You turn signals from executives, sales, customers, competitors and the engineering org into a coherent technical roadmap. You are the interpreter between “we need to detect AI exfiltration” and “here is how we instrument the endpoint to see it.”
Building for the enterprise: bulletproof and undetectable . Enterprise customers expect the Agent to be invisible to end users, resilient against tampering, and reliable in conditions that break weaker products. You own the roadmap that keeps it that way.
Performance, footprint, and reliability. Every CPU cycle, megabyte and battery percent we consume is felt by the end user and argued about by the customer's IT team. You set and defend the performance bar.
Define, measure, and meet product KPIs. Adoption, rollout velocity, deployment success rate, crash rates, detection coverage, time-to-patch on OS changes. You set the numbers and hold the team and the company to them.
Industry and ecosystem relationships. Microsoft, Apple, the Linux ecosystem, MDM vendors, and the major AV and EDR vendors. You represent Teramind in technical conversations where the agent's architecture is the subject.

5+ years of product management experience , with at least 3 owning a technical platform, SDK, agent, or systems-level product. This is a senior IC seat: influence without headcount.

Endpoint or systems background. You have shipped endpoint security (EDR, EPP, XDR), monitoring or management agents, OS-level tools, or systems software. You think in outcomes, not features. Success is “95% of customers roll out a new agent version within 30 days,” not “shipped version 27.0.”
You are comfortable with security trade-offs. Visibility versus privacy, tamper protection versus usability, cloud processing versus on-device intelligence. You can hold the attacker's perspective and the IT buyer's perspective in the same conversation.
You work with AI, not just about it. You use AI in your own practice, prototyping to pressure-test concepts before spending engineering cycles, and evaluating model behavior rather than trusting vendor claims.
You bring rigor, and you write. PRDs, decision memos, prioritization frameworks, release cadence, credible engineering-facing specs. In a distributed team, writing is how product management scales.

--------
You will own Flex's Accountants Stack. Accounting integrations, expense management, bill pay, invoicing, AR and AP, and financial reporting. The full set of tools that closely held business owners and the accountants who serve them use to run the financial operations of the company.
The accountant is the lead persona for this role. Bookkeepers, controllers, fractional CFOs, and outside CPAs are the people who actually live in this software day to day. Build for them and the owner wins by default. Build only for the owner and the accountant works around you, which means you lose.
The reason this role exists at Flex and not at every fintech is the unique customer we serve.

Super premium business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue have a controller or an outside accountant, real ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, sometimes Microsoft Dynamics or Acumatica), and a layered financial life where the business and personal sides are deeply intertwined.

The owner pays themselves a distribution, then funds personal investments, then pays for an asset, then expenses something back through the company. Their accountant has to make all of it tie out. We are the only product positioned to make that integrated life elegant for both sides. This role builds it.
You will not build a generic accounting integration. You will build the Accountants Stack that bookkeepers, controllers, and CPAs actually want, which means knowing what they hate about QuickBooks, what they love about NetSuite, what they wish Bill.com did, and where the seams between business and personal finance create the most friction today.

----------------
Define the strategy and own the connectivity layer to the accounting and ERP systems our customers' accountants use. QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, etc.
Build expense management that works for owners and the accountants reconciling on their behalf. Receipt capture, GL coding, approval workflows, integration into the accounting tools without requiring manual reconciliation downstream.
Own bill pay and AR/AP. The workflow from invoice received to vendor paid, from invoice sent to customer paid, with full reconciliation back to the accounting system.
Build the invoicing product. We do not have a real invoicing offering today and customers are starting to ask. Decide what shape it takes and ship it.
Architect the connection between business financial data and personal financial data. This is the wedge no other fintech has. Make the integrated owner life real in product so the accountant can deliver it cleanly.
Partner closely with the Banking, Credit, Cards, and Payments product owners so financial flows tie out cleanly across the stack. No seams. No reconciliation tax for the accountant or the customer.
Translate the controller, CFO, and CPA persona for the rest of the company. We need someone who speaks both owner and accountant fluently. And can translate it to the owner mindset.
What you will need
------------------
You have spent years thinking about how business owners and the accountants who serve them actually run financial operations. You know the difference between a bookkeeper, a controller, a fractional CFO, and an outside accountant, and you have built product for at least one of them.
Deep, hands-on familiarity with at least two of: QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica. Not "I know they exist." Actually built in or integrated to them at depth.
You can journal a transaction without looking it up. You understand accrual versus cash basis, the close cycle, what a 1099 is for, and why a controller cares about the audit trail.
You have built either inside an accounting platform, on top of one as an integration partner, or built a fintech product that lives natively in the accounting workflow.
You understand the accountant channel and how CPAs influence product adoption. Bonus if you have built for or partnered with CPAs directly.
Typically 4 to 10 years of experience. Title is not the point.

We want to hear from you. We value passion, determination, and honesty. If you do not match every line of the spec but you can show us the work, apply anyway. Unusual paths and rare skills are how you stand out at Flex.

Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well.
We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology already powers some of the UK’s most ambitious fintechs, banks, financial advisers and wealth firms, with close to a million investors relying on Seccl-powered platforms. And we’re now expanding into Europe.
We’ve got a proven product, strong momentum and big ambitions for what comes next: helping more household-name brands launch and scale investment propositions, entering new markets and replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for scale.
We’re proud to be part of Octopus, one of the UK’s most successful privately held investment and technology groups. That gives us the backing and long-term perspective to build something substantial, while keeping the pace and energy of a high-growth business. Seccl and Octopus are both B Corp certified and share a belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand.
If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and across Europe, you’ll be in good company.
Check out the Seccl website to see what we’re building and read more about our mission to shape the future of investments.

We’re looking for a Group product manager to join our product team. This role sits at the heart of the Seccl platform, shaping the core capabilities that our clients rely on to build and scale their investment propositions. You’ll focus on delivering a stable, flexible platform while continuously improving the experience for both adviser and fintech clients.
You’ll work closely with clients to understand their needs, translating them into clear product direction and ensuring we’re building solutions that support a wide range of business models and customer journeys. From core platform capabilities to client-facing experiences, your domain will play a critical role in how firms deliver value to their end investors.
You won’t lead a single squad day-to-day. Instead, you’ll lead multiple Product managers across several squads, setting direction, aligning priorities, and driving strategic initiatives across your domain. You’ll work closely with two other GPMs to shape the end-to-end platform roadmap.
On a typical day you will…
Set the vision and strategy for your tribe area, shaping direction 6-18 months ahead
Build and maintain clear, coherent roadmaps that balance short-term delivery with long-term impact
Develop strong relationships with advisers, developers and firms, deeply understanding their workflows, pain points and needs
Lead, coach and support Product Managers, helping them grow, prioritise effectively, and deliver meaningful outcomes
Work closely with engineering leadership to deliver scalable, reliable, compliant platform capabilities
Drive alignment across squads, ensuring shared context, cross-functional collaboration and consistency of approach
Champion customer-centric product decisions through continuous discovery, data-driven insights and tight feedback loops
Collaborate with commercial, operations, support and compliance teams to balance current and future customer needs with business opportunities.
Promote operational excellence, improving processes that impact experience and efficiency
Contribute to product culture, shaping how we scale our ways of working as the organisation grows. Act as one product leadership with the two other Group Product Managers
This role’s for you if you..
Have experience leading multiple squads or teams within a high-growth, API-first, fintech, or regulated environment
Are a strategic thinker, balancing long-term vision with execution.
Have a strong commercial mindset, understanding how product decisions impact business growth.
Can build deep relationships with customers, acting as their advocate within the business.
Are an excellent people leader, coaching and mentoring product managers to excel.
Have a track record of improving processes and driving operational efficiencies.
Work closely with engineering leadership, ensuring a strong product-engineering partnership.
Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, using data to drive decisions.

Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams. With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remoters working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote.
With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role.
We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform.
If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work!
What this job can offer you
Own the technical implementation of our Marketing Operations Foundations program - our strategic marketing processes and products that enable how Remote acquires, nurtures, serves, and grows customers. Work with Marketing Ops, Sales, Customer Success, Engineering, Data, and Legal to translate strategic requirements into scalable technical solutions.

Define product strategy, architecture, and roadmaps while treating business systems as products rather than standalone tools.

Build and ship GTM products and features using AI tools
Partner with stakeholders across Revenue Operations, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Business Systems, Data, AI, and Engineering to deliver scalable business capabilities.
Shape the future of Remote's Revenue Technology ecosystem by continuously improving the products that power our go-to-market organization.

Experience leading or managing complex, multi-month technical initiatives involving cross-functional teams, with proven ability to break down ambiguous problems into executable roadmaps.

Drive decisions without bulldozing. People won't always agree on priorities. It's your job to land decisions while keeping people bought in.
Close the loop. After we ship, help the team understand the impact.

Du bist unser erster Product Manager – das Bindegewebe zwischen Engineering und Business. Founding-Rolle mit Owner-Mentalität über den gesamten Produktlebenszyklus: die richtige Mischung aus Produktmanagement, Produktmarketing und strategischer Vision. Ajaia is an AI implementation consultancy and product studio. We help organizations move from AI experimentation to measurable return on investment across four practices: AI Strategy and Advisory, Workforce Training and Enablement, Process Optimization, and Custom AI Development. Our work sits with executives and the people who do the work, and it is judged on whether something changed in production, not on whether a pilot looked good in a deck.

Ajaia is hiring a remote Product Manager to own products in Ajaia's product suite end to end. You will talk to users and customers every week, decide what gets built next and why, and say plainly what does not get built, including when the loudest voice in the room wants it.

You will write specs an engineer can build from without a follow-up meeting, prototype with AI tools when a working demo settles an argument faster than a deck, and stay on the number after launch and act on what it tells you. This is a builder's seat: you will contribute to the code and the design yourself, not only direct them.
You will work with a US-based team and US clients. Most of your users, stakeholders, and engineers sit in New York, so this role is built around daily overlap with US Eastern hours, not asynchronous handoffs.
Compensation: Competitive, benchmarked to senior product roles in your market, plus a performance bonus tied to product outcomes. We will share a specific number for your location early in the process.
How we expect you to work
AI use is a core execution requirement at Ajaia, not optional tooling. You will use AI daily to sort through usage data, draft specs, and build working prototypes yourself, and you are judged on what you keep from that output, not on how much of it you generated. The tools change fast, and staying current on what is worth using is part of the job.
Remote works here when the writing is strong. Decisions, specs, and priority calls get written down where the team can read them, not held in your head until the next call.

Talk to users and customers every week. Not a quarterly survey. Real conversations, real usage, on US time.
Turn messy, sometimes contradictory signal, usage data, support tickets, sales requests, and what people say in interviews, into a ranked call on what gets built next.
Say plainly what does not get built, including a well-funded customer's request, when the evidence does not support it.
Write specs an engineer can build from without a follow-up meeting: the outcome, what is in and out of scope, where a human stays in the loop, and acceptance criteria someone could test.
Prototype the core flow yourself, wireframes, a clickable mock, or a working demo, when that settles the argument faster than a deck would.
Contribute to the code and the design directly: ship a small feature or fix with AI tools, mock the screen yourself, and hand engineers something running instead of something described.
Partner with the design team on what the solution should be and how it holds up for the people using it.
Partner with the delivery team and engineers on how the build runs and the date it ships by.
Present the roadmap and the tradeoffs to the people who fund it, including when a client or a salesperson is unhappy with the call.
Hold a priority decision under real pushback, or change it, and say why either way.
Ship it, then watch the number after launch and act on what it says.

Highly organized across multiple priorities and open questions at once.
Sharp judgment on what to build next, and clear about what not to build.
Strong plain written and spoken English: specs and decisions other people can act on without a follow-up meeting, and customer calls you can run without a translator.
AI fluent: you use AI daily to sort signal, draft specs, and prototype, and you can tell good output from slop.
Comfortable contributing to code and design directly, with AI tools making you faster at both.
Comfortable holding a priority call under pushback, or changing it for stated reasons.
1 or more years in product management, or work that proves the same skill.
Available for at least 7 to 8 hours of daily overlap with US Eastern time (9am to 6pm ET), consistently.
Reliable internet, a quiet place to take customer calls, and your own laptop.
Legally able to work as an independent contractor or through an employer of record in your country.

Prior experience working remotely with a US or UK team.
Experience with a B2B product used by an operational or compliance function.
Comfort reading usage data or a support queue yourself.
Exposure to a regulated industry such as financial services, insurance, healthcare, or legal.
Prior experience in a 0-to-1 or early-stage product role.

Our team is working to define the “canonical stack” for AI workflows, by solving the toughest problems in AI today: how to experiment, evaluate, understand and improve models or applications at scale in a responsible way.

The product team has deep technical and strategic backgrounds from leading AI/ML companies (Uber, Cruise, Spotify, Apple) and experience shipping market leading platforms at scale.

Working with this team is an opportunity to develop further as a PM leader in a rapidly growing space by collaborating with some of the best in class AI Engineers and Data Scientists in the industry.

You will be owning, strategizing, and developing a large portion of Arize AI ’s core product roadmap.
From ideation to creation, you will be involved in all stages of the product life cycle.
You will be engaging with our customers directly to gather meaningful insight and feedback in order to create a world class product.
You will be working cross functionally with internal and external stakeholders; including engineering, design, marketing, and sales to drive our product strategy into production.
You will be responsible for communicating and integrating competitive analysis, usability research, and market analysis into product requirements.
Utilize your understanding in AI/ML/CV or related technical space in order to contribute to Arize AI ’s main product offering.

* Zum Herzstück: Als Product Owner verantwortest du die Website css.ch und steuerst ihre Weiterentwicklung entlang der Unternehmens- und Digitalstrategie.

Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you’ve probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it.

We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We’re approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical.

We’re a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

We’re looking for a highly technical, systems-minded Senior Product Manager to lead two critical search intelligence teams: Machine Learning & Recall and Query . Search at Constructor is fundamentally an ML challenge, and this role sits at the absolute entry point of our discovery pipeline, right where shopper intent meets candidate retrieval.
In this role, you will bridge the Query team (understanding what a shopper means across intent, entities, and language) with the Machine Learning & Recall team (retrieving the exact right set of candidate products across massive catalogs).

You will define strategy across both domains, balancing state-of-the-art techniques, such as vector search, semantic parsing, dense embeddings, and LLM-assisted query interpretation, with low-latency production execution.

You won’t be measured on shipping features for the sake of it; you’ll be measured on candidate quality, query accuracy, and driving business outcomes like conversion rate, search-attributed revenue, and revenue per visit.

Set a unified roadmap: Define the multi-quarter vision and strategy across both the Machine Learning & Recall and Query teams, ensuring query understanding and candidate generation evolve hand-in-hand.
Drive Query intelligence: Lead the Query team to push boundaries in tokenization, spell correction, entity extraction, intent classification, and LLM-assisted query parsing across multiple languages.
Advance Recall systems: Lead the Machine Learning & Recall team in evolving candidate generation architecture, seamlessly combining traditional keyword search with modern dense embeddings, vector retrieval, and hybrid recall models.
Move core business metrics: Own measurable lift in search-attributed conversion, revenue per visit, and GMV across all retail customer verticals.
Turn research into production wins: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with ML researchers, data scientists, and software engineers to take SOTA models from research to low-latency, cost-effective production systems.
Balance ML performance trade-offs: Make data-backed decisions balancing model complexity, accuracy, inference latency, compute costs, and real-time execution constraints.
Build evaluation frameworks: Establish robust offline and online measurement systems to evaluate retrieval precision and query understanding accuracy against customer revenue outcomes.
Orchestrate pipeline handoffs: Ensure candidate product sets and query context flow cleanly into downstream ranking and search quality models without signal loss.
Solve systemic issues: Lead technical triage when query interpretation or retrieval anomalies occur, building durable, automated fixes rather than one-off patches.
What Success Looks Like

Driven quantifiable lift in search-attributed conversion and revenue per visit across major customer verticals.
Stood up an integrated evaluation framework connecting query parsing and candidate recall directly to business outcomes.
Optimized inference latency and compute infrastructure to ensure high-capacity ML models run fast and cost-effectively in production.

About Magic Eden and Dicey
Magic Eden reached unicorn status in just 9 months after launch, one of the fastest in history. We built a category-defining NFT marketplace from scratch and proved we know how to move fast. Now we're doing it again. Dicey is our crypto casino and sportsbook platform, targeting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets.
We're a small, fully remote team. We ship fast, we're hands-on with our data, and we're rebuilding how a growth team operates around AI from the ground up.

Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.
This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. It's explicitly AI-native. You'll build workflows, agents, and pipelines to run lifecycle campaigns that would have taken a whole team two years ago. Half the job is identifying the right problem. The other half is running the experiments to find the answer.

Own retention and monetization as a growth loop. Set the targets, find the leverage, and drive the numbers for everything that happens after a player signs up
Own the player segmentation framework. Today it's value and risk. You decide how it evolves, what signals feed it, and how the rest of the company uses it
Build the AI-native growth stack. Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work
Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Size them, spec them, ship them, measure them
Spend real time in our data warehouse and on-chain data finding patterns and turn them into campaigns before anyone else does
Expand the signals we have on players: on-chain activity, status-match programs, social account linking, and whatever else you can think of
Run the campaigns. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting
Partner with engineering and design to ship the product surfaces that make all of this repeatable
